resolved.question: Layer C concurrency model: cargo runs against committed code. Two main options to avoid contention with a running impl-task on the same worktree: (a) tmp-dir clone — git clone phase-branch into /tmp/validate-<sha>/ each run, run cargo there; (b) worktree-reuse — cargo runs in the existing phase-branch worktree, blocked by flock if impl-task is editing.
options: (a) tmp-dir clone — robust, cold cargo cache per run
(b) worktree-reuse with flock — fast, risk of file conflicts
(c) Hybrid: tmp-dir for first run, worktree-reuse for retries
(d) Shared target dir + tmp-dir source
resolved.context: Source: validate-agent-design.md §9.2(4) + §8 'Failure modes to design against'. Judgment-heavy — affects validate-runner's robustness model + cold-cache cost per validation. Brief recommends option (a). Cargo cache penalty is one-time per phase since /tmp/validate-* dirs persist within a sub-phase (validate-runner can keep CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/validate-<phase>/target/ as a phase-scoped shared cache, deleting only on phase close). Worktree-reuse fails when an impl-task pre-commit edit overlaps validate's read.
resolved.answer: (a) tmp-dir clone (per user 2026-04-27). Each validate run does `git clone --shared --branch <commit_sha> /tmp/validate-<sha>/`, sets CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/validate-<phase>/target/ (shared across runs within a phase to keep cargo cache warm), runs cargo there, deletes the source dir after (target dir persists until phase close). Robust: zero risk of clobbering an in-flight impl-task. The cargo cache penalty is mitigated by phase-scoped target dir reuse — cold cache only on first validation per phase. Reasoning supplemental to user choice: option (d) shared target dir was rejected because cargo's incremental compilation state isn't robust under concurrent writes. Option (b) flock has a hidden failure mode where validate queues indefinitely behind a stuck impl-task. Option (c) hybrid adds run-mode logic to validate-runner unnecessarily.
